inspection.type:
∀ (l : ℕ),
  2 ≤ l + 1 →
    ∀ {α : ℝ},
      0 ≤ α →
        α / 2 < 2 - 1 / ↑(l + 1) →
          ∃ d,
            0 < d ∧
              (∀ᶠ (t : ℕ) in Filter.atTop,
                  d * ↑(QuarticQuery.mValue t) ^ (2 - 1 / ↑(l + 1) - α / 2) /
                      Real.logb 2 ↑(QuarticQuery.mValue t) ^ (2 + α * 6) ≤
                    ↑(QuarticQuery.R
                          (QuarticQuery.totalise
                            (QuarticQuery.Fkm (l + 1) t (QuarticQuery.Forrelation.forrCircuit l t)))) /
                      (1 +
                          ↑(QuarticQuery.Q
                              (QuarticQuery.totalise
                                (QuarticQuery.Fkm (l + 1) t (QuarticQuery.Forrelation.forrCircuit l t))))) ^
                        α) ∧
                Filter.Tendsto
                    (fun t =>
                      d * ↑(QuarticQuery.mValue t) ^ (2 - 1 / ↑(l + 1) - α / 2) /
                        Real.logb 2 ↑(QuarticQuery.mValue t) ^ (2 + α * 6))
                    Filter.atTop Filter.atTop ∧
                  Filter.Tendsto
                    (fun t =>
                      ↑(QuarticQuery.R
                            (QuarticQuery.totalise
                              (QuarticQuery.Fkm (l + 1) t (QuarticQuery.Forrelation.forrCircuit l t)))) /
                        (1 +
                            ↑(QuarticQuery.Q
                                (QuarticQuery.totalise
                                  (QuarticQuery.Fkm (l + 1) t (QuarticQuery.Forrelation.forrCircuit l t))))) ^
                          α)
                    Filter.atTop Filter.atTop

lean.note: The type supplies one fixed circuit family, a positive constant, explicit b_k=6, the eventual quotient bound, and divergence of both lower envelope and quotient.

hypotheses: hQ, hR: eventual bounds on the two sequences
lean.note: Abstract sequences: eventually R_t > D(1+Q_t)^alpha for every D. The ratio's explicit lower bound is not stated.
open_assumptions: hQ, hR: eventual bounds on the two sequences

presentation.body: For fixed $0\le\alpha<4$ and integer $k\ge 2$ with $2-1/k>\alpha/2$: $\frac{R(F_{k,m})}{(1+Q(F_{k,m}))^\alpha}\ge\frac{c_{k,\alpha}m^{2-1/k-\alpha/2}}{(\log m)^{2+\alpha b_k}}$, which tends to infinity.
presentation.body_plain: For fixed 0 ≤ α < 4 and integer k ≥ 2 with 2−1/k > α/2: R(Fₖ,ₘ)/(1+Q(Fₖ,ₘ))^α ≥ cₖ,α m^(2−1/k−α/2)/(log m)^(2+αbₖ), which tends to infinity.
presentation.title: Every smaller exponent gives an unbounded ratio
presentation.title_plain: Every smaller exponent gives an unbounded ratio

statement: For fixed 0<=alpha<4 and integer k>=2 with 2-1/k>alpha/2: R(F_{k,m})/(1+Q(F_{k,m}))^alpha >= c_{k,alpha} m^{2-1/k-alpha/2}/(log m)^{2+alpha b_k}, which tends to infinity.
